target_effect: Reduced-form effect of invoice introduction on sales/output, employment, investment, exit and supplier relationships
policy_variation: National introduction on 2023-10-01 interacted with pre-treatment B2B exposure to exempt/non-registered suppliers
treatment_or_exposure: Freeze exposure using only pre-2023 supplier links and pre-treatment VAT/exemption status; never classify treatment using post-2023 registration choices
comparison_group: Lower-exposure firms within common pre-treatment industry/size/region support
required_microdata: 2021-2025+ firm outcomes; pre-2023 supplier-customer links and transaction values; pre-treatment VAT/exemption status; stable firm IDs; industry/size/region; invoice registration history for diagnostics only
main_threats: Exposure correlated with differential trends; anticipation before 2023-10; COVID/reopening and sector shocks; network rewiring before treatment; missing sole proprietors; linkage selection
required_diagnostics: Dynamic event-study coefficients; joint pre-trend test; placebo 2022 treatment date; covariate/exposure overlap; frozen pre-treatment exposure audit; sensitivity to industry-by-time controls; attrition/linkage bounds
stop_rule: Do not estimate using post-treatment registration or post-treatment supplier composition as the exposure. Stop if no pre-2023 supplier/VAT-status network can be lawfully linked to repeated outcomes.
next_step: Request an approved firm/network panel or provider-confirmed secure link containing pre-2023 supplier exposure and 2021-2025+ outcomes.

target_effect: Marginal seller-side effect of invoice-related tax burden relief on small registered businesses; mechanism evidence for invoice burden, not the full 2023 introduction effect
policy_variation: Current 20-percent special measure ends; individual proprietors alone receive a 30-percent special measure for 2027-2028 while corporations do not
treatment_or_exposure: Pre-policy legal form × ex-ante eligibility for the special measure; align treatment to each tax period rather than calendar date
comparison_group: Comparable eligible small corporations and ineligible/less-affected groups with overlapping pre-period outcomes
required_microdata: 2024-2028 individual + corporation VAT/tax panel; special-measure eligibility/use; base-period taxable sales; legal form; sales/income; employment/investment/exit if linkable; stable longitudinal IDs
main_threats: Legal-form noncomparability; self-selection into incorporation; simultaneous 2026 invoice reforms; simple-taxation switching; different fiscal-year timing; differential macro shocks
required_diagnostics: Pre-trend/event-study; common-support matching/reweighting; eligibility triple difference; fiscal-period alignment; simplified-taxation transition controls; placebo on earlier periods; legal-form-specific trend robustness
stop_rule: Do not interpret a raw individual-vs-corporation difference as causal. Require overlapping pre-trends and exact eligibility/tax-period coding.
next_step: Freeze the analysis protocol before 2027 outcomes mature; identify an approved data route covering both sole proprietors and corporations.

target_effect: Buyer-side effect on supplier retention, prices, purchases and firm outcomes from reduced input-credit relief for purchases from non-qualified issuers
policy_variation: From 2026-10 the transitional input-credit share changes from 80% to 70%; the per-supplier purchase cap also tightens from 1bn to 100m yen for affected tax periods
treatment_or_exposure: Pre-step share/value of purchases from non-qualified issuers, frozen before 2026-10; cap exposure coded separately
comparison_group: Firms with lower pre-step non-qualified-supplier exposure and/or transactions safely below the new cap
required_microdata: 2025-2028 buyer-supplier transaction panel with supplier invoice status, purchase amounts, buyer outcomes and tax-period dates; stable IDs; cap exposure
main_threats: Anticipatory network rewiring; simultaneous cap change; policy anticipation; transaction-specific exceptions; exposure measurement error; industry shocks
required_diagnostics: Event-study pre-trends; frozen-exposure audit; separate cap-affected strata; placebo thresholds/dates; supplier fixed effects where possible; robustness excluding special-exception transactions
stop_rule: Do not use an 80-to-50 treatment contrast: the current 2026 reform changed the first step to 80-to-70. Do not combine the share and cap shocks without separate exposure coding.
next_step: Pre-specify post-2026 collection now and obtain transaction-level/provider data; first post-period estimate only after adequate outcome horizon.

target_effect: Association/local effect of invoice registration timing on firm outcomes if a valid exogenous timing/comparison device can be added
policy_variation: Public invoice registration/expiration/cancellation history linked to BSBSA outcomes
comparison_group: Not valid from never/late registrants alone without a defensible instrument or predetermined exposure
required_microdata: Approved BSBSA panel with privacy-preserving corporation key + public invoice registry history
main_threats: Endogenous registration; business-model selection; exit-related registration changes; BSBSA coverage; sole-proprietor exclusion
required_diagnostics: Pre-trends; registration hazard model; event-time balance; placebo dates; never treat endogenous timing as natural experiment by itself
stop_rule: Do not report a causal registration effect from a naive registered-vs-unregistered or early-vs-late event study.
next_step: Use only as linkage backbone for design rank 1 or another exogenous policy margin; otherwise retain as diagnostic.

target_effect: Local change in firm behavior around the VAT exemption threshold after invoice introduction
treatment_or_exposure: Threshold proximity using the legally relevant base-period taxable-sales concept and invoice-era rules
comparison_group: Firms locally around the threshold with pre/post difference-in-discontinuities or explicit bunching model
required_microdata: Longitudinal VAT/tax records with legally correct base-period sales, current sales/outcomes, registration/tax status and firm ID
main_threats: Strategic bunching/manipulation; two-year base-period lag; voluntary registration; concurrent relief measures; discontinuous composition; current-vs-base sales mismatch
required_diagnostics: Density/bunching test; donut/bandwidth sensitivity; pre-reform placebo thresholds; exact legal threshold mapping; separate registered/exempt composition; continuity diagnostics
stop_rule: Do not run a conventional RDD if the running variable is manipulable without explicitly modeling bunching/manipulation and base-period timing.
next_step: Keep as a future NTA restricted-data design; reuse historical bunching methods and treat results as local unless transport is separately justified.
